correctness.rationale: The generating function F_k=P D^(k−1), with D=prod(1+q^m), satisfies D(q)^7≡D(q^7) in characteristic 7. Thus both infinite progression vanishing and vanishing of its first two terms depend only on k modulo 7. An exact 7×14 integer coefficient calculation finds precisely five simultaneous-zero residue pairs, with explicit first-two obstructions to all others; published Hirschhorn–Sellers Theorem 1.3 proves all five positive infinite families. k=3,r=6 has initial zero but next coefficient 1, proving two is the sharp uniform sample count. Independent coefficient computation matched all 98 canonical residues; infinite implication rests on formal identity and cited theorem, not computation alone.
